criteria.criterion: `## The driver` is the heading right after `## The loop` in docs/guide/concepts.md: the driver is `vloop run` itself, the deterministic half; it plans nothing and judges nothing; it starts every session, runs every gate and check, owns every status change and makes every commit, and is the boundary the permission fence only advises on (exit 9); a table or list says who does what — the driver; the plan, gate-review, work and review sessions; the operator
criteria.evidence: concepts.md:16 '## The driver' follows '## The loop' (line 6); text and who-does-what table cover driver, four sessions and operator; exit 9 matches domain-model.md:201

criteria.criterion: Violation: any sentence stating the driver plans, judges or reviews, or contradicting the glossary's driver, P-2, S-2 or R-1 (e.g. a session committing or setting status, the driver writing gate folders)
criteria.evidence: table says the driver never plans/judges/reviews; sessions never commit or set status; the plan session writes the gate folder

criteria.criterion: "Setting up a repository" says go install never touches PATH, gives `export PATH="$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin"`, and the file per shell: zsh `~/.zprofile` (or `~/.zshrc`), bash `~/.bash_profile` on macOS and `~/.profile` on most Linux, PowerShell the user Path variable (the Go MSI installer usually adds `%USERPROFILE%\go\bin`; otherwise field note 7's `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable` line, preferred over `$PROFILE` because it reaches cmd and apps too)
criteria.evidence: concepts.md ~291-308 in 'Setting up a repository' has the export line, per-shell files, MSI note and the SetEnvironmentVariable line with the preference reason

criteria.criterion: Where the plugin is described: vloop run's sessions load the plugin it hands them and not the plugins enabled in the user's settings (measured 2026-10-11); for interactive sessions install the plugin or pass --plugin-dir, not both. Violation: any claim about what Claude Code does with two plugins of one name
criteria.evidence: paragraph after the --plugin-dir example states exactly this, with no claim about same-name plugins

criteria.criterion: Where the gate folder is described: state.json, plan.md and .vloop/state/gates/ belong to the current plan; vloop brief close keeps them; they are replaced when the next brief is planned or when a new plan is rejected as unfit; earlier plans' gate folders live in git history
criteria.evidence: 'Gate fixtures' paragraph in concepts.md states all of these

criteria.criterion: The doctor paragraph lists the `gate edits` check and says the plugin check warns when no vloop plugin is installed
criteria.evidence: doctor paragraph lists 'the plugin (a warning when no vloop plugin is installed), `gate edits` (a warning...)'

criteria.criterion: `## Retiring the shell loop`: remove .claude/skills/loop-plan, loop-work and loop-review, the `<!-- loop:begin -->…<!-- loop:end -->` block in CLAUDE.md (moving any rule vloop's section lacks — the shell loop's rule 1 on ~/.claude — into the repository's own part), .claude/loop-knowledge.md and .loop/tmp/; keep .loop/state/ with a one-line .loop/RETIRED.md, because vloop reads its state.json and runs/ for metrics and defects; the rest of .loop/ stays in git history
criteria.evidence: concepts.md:352 section lists every removal, the rule-1 move, and keeping .loop/state/ with RETIRED.md

criteria.criterion: Neither docs/guide/concepts.md nor docs/guide/metrics.md says the legacy layout is read 'in this repository only'; they say vloop reads .loop/state/ in any repository that has it
criteria.evidence: diff replaces both phrasings (concepts.md legacy paragraph, metrics.md run folders bullet)
